facts.text: A weekly transit pass is often better value than several individual day tickets if staying 4+ days; trams and the U-Bahn cover the center comprehensively.
Viennese coffeehouse culture expects you to linger — a single coffee (€4-6) buys the table for hours; it isn't rude to sit long, but it does mean a coffeehouse isn't a "quick stop."

Restaurants directly on Stephansplatz or immediately around the Hofburg charge a notable premium for standard Austrian dishes (schnitzel, goulash) versus a few streets into the Innere Stadt or the Naschmarkt area.

The Schönbrunn Palace gardens are free to enter; only the palace interior and certain garden features (maze, gloriette) require paid tickets — easy to accidentally overpay by not distinguishing these.
Jaywalking is culturally frowned upon and can be fined; Viennese pedestrians reliably wait for the signal even with no traffic present.
Traditional Viennese cuisine is heavy (schnitzel, sausages, pastries); vegetarian options are increasingly available in the center but far more limited in traditional Beisl (tavern) settings.
